Each time it nacks the message and it gets redelivered over and over (attempt 6, then 15, then 23), because no max-retries is configured. Partition 2 stops moving forward, and lag grows from 610 to 4348 messages (46s to 344s). That fits the alert: lag is rising but CPU is normal, because the worker spends its time retrying one message instead of doing heavy work. Before this, batches were processed with lag under 400ms. The search-api 'timed out waiting for downstream confirmation' errors come after the stall and are a downstream effect. I found no warnings or errors in catalog-svc, catalog-db or redis-cache.
The NUL byte suggests the producer may have written a corrupted payload. Even so, the failure that is stalling the queue is a single poison message being redelivered.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-185456 (partition 2, offset 161402) to a dead-letter queue or skip it so partition 2 starts moving again. Set a max-retries limit with dead-lettering on the index-worker consumer. Check how catalog-svc produced a payload with a NUL byte, then fix it and reprocess the message.
